strengths: The paper addresses a relevant problem for speech language models: obtaining high-quality acoustic representations with fewer codebooks. Its combination of masked parallel quantization, residual refinement, and Fourier-based decoding has a clear practical motivation.

Reconstruction experiments cover LibriTTS Test-Clean, Test-Other, and LJSpeech, with multiple complementary metrics. The reported improvements are substantial: at four codebooks, LibriTTS Test-Clean PESQ increases from 2.4026 for Vocos to 3.1188 for Language-Codec.

Downstream evaluation includes both autoregressive VALL-E and parallel MobileSpeech. Crucially, the MCRVQ ablation holds other training configurations fixed and retrains the downstream models. Speaker similarity improves from 0.6403 to 0.6806 and from 0.7085 to 0.7544, respectively, supporting a benefit from the proposed component.

The manuscript links code and pretrained models and documents substantial training and evaluation details. Together with the reconstruction results and controlled downstream ablation, this supports a useful empirical contribution suitable for Findings.
weaknesses: The central explanation—that MCRVQ redistributes information and makes acoustic tokens easier to predict from text—is not directly established. There are no channel-wise information, prediction-loss, or convergence measurements. Since reconstruction performance is not reported for the controlled MCRVQ ablation, its downstream gains cannot distinguish easier token modeling from improved codec fidelity.

The reconstruction comparisons establish the performance of the complete system but do not isolate contributions from the larger dataset, decoder, discriminators, and quantizer. In particular, attributing the Language-Codec–Vocos difference to MCRVQ is unjustified. Comparisons with the cited HiFi-Codec and improved RVQGAN/DAC are also missing, limiting the broad state-of-the-art claim.

The claimed downstream efficiency is insufficiently evaluated. Tables 3–5 omit the quantizer counts and bitrates used, and no latency, memory, or generation-cost measurements are provided. Strong four-codebook reconstruction alone does not demonstrate improved downstream efficiency.

The method description needs greater precision. Equation (5) equates masking with division by Nq, and Equation (7) does not clearly implement the accumulated residual described in the text. Tensor shapes, mask construction, and fusion need explicit specification. Missing architectural and loss settings, together with 20,000 hours of private training data, limit reproduction from the manuscript alone despite the linked artifacts.

The scope and uncertainty of the evidence require more cautious claims. Objective results lack variability estimates, CMOS differences lack uncertainty and a sufficiently detailed protocol, and several MOS gains over Encodec+Vocos are small. Evaluation is restricted to English speech and short prompted continuations; single-speaker LJSpeech and the Test-Other split provide limited evidence for broader domain, multilingual, or noise robustness.
